{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "An unset judge-server token becomes a publicly predictable authentication credential",
      "rule": "Fail closed when configuring service authentication",
      "cwe": "CWE-287",
      "severity": "high",
      "confidence": "high",
      "attacker": "An unauthenticated network client when JUDGE_SERVER_TOKEN is unset or empty in the supplied container deployment.",
      "invariant": "Only authorized judge servers may register service destinations, receive submitted programs, and supply verdicts.",
      "source_to_sink": "The startup script unconditionally interpolates JUDGE_SERVER_TOKEN into a Python assignment. An unset variable therefore overwrites the randomly generated option with an empty string. The public, CSRF-exempt heartbeat endpoint accepts SHA-256 of that empty value. An attacker can consequently register or update a JudgeServer with an attacker-controlled service_url, maintain its heartbeat, and become eligible for ChooseJudgeServer. JudgeDispatcher then sends submitted source and problem configuration to that destination and trusts its verdict response. The same destination control permits backend POST requests to reachable internal HTTP services.",
      "impact": "Judge-server authentication bypass, submitted-code disclosure, forged judging results, and server-side HTTP requests. This source does not establish operating-system code execution.",
      "locations": [
        {"file": "deploy/entrypoint.sh", "start_line": 61, "end_line": 64},
        {"file": "options/options.py", "start_line": 90, "end_line": 92},
        {"file": "conf/views.py", "start_line": 132, "end_line": 159},
        {"file": "judge/dispatcher.py", "start_line": 38, "end_line": 47},
        {"file": "judge/dispatcher.py", "start_line": 141, "end_line": 174}
      ],
      "source_snippets": [
        "echo \"from options.options import SysOptions; SysOptions.judge_server_token='$JUDGE_SERVER_TOKEN'\" | python manage.py shell &&",
        "return token if token else rand_str()",
        "if hashlib.sha256(SysOptions.judge_server_token.encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest() != client_token:",
        "server.service_url = data[\"service_url\"]",
        "resp = self._request(urljoin(server.service_url, \"/judge\"), data=data)"
      ],
      "counterevidence": "The Python option initializer generates a cryptographically random fallback, but the later startup assignment replaces it. Supplying a strong nonempty environment token prevents this specific bypass. No external deployment configuration or live environment was inspected.",
      "remediation": "Reject missing or empty service tokens before starting the application, or preserve a securely generated persistent token rather than assigning an empty value. Avoid shell interpolation into Python source. Treat configured judge destinations as an explicit service trust boundary."
    },
    {
      "title": "Problem-copy endpoints bypass source and destination ownership checks",
      "rule": "Authorize every source and destination object in a copy operation",
      "cwe": "CWE-862",
      "severity": "high",
      "confidence": "high",
      "attacker": "An ordinary Admin account, including one whose problem_permission is None for AddContestProblemAPI.",
      "invariant": "An Admin may manage only authorized problems and contests; hidden contest problems and their test cases must remain private.",
      "source_to_sink": "AddContestProblemAPI accepts caller-controlled contest_id and problem_id, fetches both without ownership, visibility, public-state, or problem-permission restrictions, and clones the problem into the selected contest. An Admin can create an owned contest, clone a hidden problem from somebody else's contest into it, then legitimately use ContestProblemAPI.get and TestCaseAPI.get to retrieve the cloned problem's full fields and original test-case files. The same missing destination check allows adding problems to another administrator's ongoing or future contest. MakeContestProblemPublicAPIView similarly fetches an arbitrary contest problem by id and changes its is_public state without authorizing its owner.",
      "impact": "Disclosure of private problem statements, hidden templates, special-judge source and test cases; unauthorized contest modification and problem-publication state changes.",
      "locations": [
        {"file": "problem/views/admin.py", "start_line": 471, "end_line": 495},
        {"file": "problem/views/admin.py", "start_line": 440, "end_line": 466},
        {"file": "problem/views/admin.py", "start_line": 348, "end_line": 358},
        {"file": "problem/views/admin.py", "start_line": 117, "end_line": 143},
        {"file": "account/middleware.py", "start_line": 36, "end_line": 41}
      ],
      "source_snippets": [
        "contest = Contest.objects.get(id=data[\"contest_id\"])",
        "problem = Problem.objects.get(id=data[\"problem_id\"])",
        "problem.pk = None\n        problem.contest = contest\n        problem.is_public = True\n        problem.visible = True",
        "problem = Problem.objects.get(id=data[\"id\"])",
        "problem.is_public = True\n        problem.save()",
        "ensure_created_by(problem.contest, user)",
        "ensure_created_by(problem.contest, request.user)"
      ],
      "counterevidence": "AdminRoleRequiredMiddleware excludes ordinary users. Other problem and contest endpoints use ensure_created_by, showing the intended per-owner restriction. The copy endpoints check contest end state and duplicate display IDs, but neither check authorizes the objects. Cloning preserves the original created_by, yet the downstream contest endpoints authorize the new contest owner and therefore still expose the copied data.",
      "remediation": "Authorize the destination contest before copying. Restrict public-problem imports to authorized, visible, non-contest sources, or explicitly authorize the source owner. Apply ensure_created_by to make-public operations and enforce problem_permission consistently."
    },
    {
      "title": "Shared permission-decorator state can authorize one request using another request's user",
      "rule": "Keep request-specific authorization state local to each invocation",
      "cwe": "CWE-362",
      "severity": "high",
      "confidence": "medium",
      "attacker": "An ordinary Admin sending concurrent requests while a Super Admin accesses the same decorated method; analogous races affect login and problem permissions.",
      "invariant": "A permission decision must use the same request and principal passed to the protected view.",
      "source_to_sink": "Class-based decorators are instantiated once when their view methods are defined. Their __get__ returns a partial referencing that shared instance. __call__ assigns args[1] to self.request, then check_permission and the disabled-account check read that mutable field. In a threaded worker, another invocation can replace self.request between assignment and authorization. The original invocation can pass a Super Admin permission check using the concurrent privileged request and then call self.func with its original attacker-controlled args. UserAdminAPI.put is one sensitive consumer and can change passwords and administrative roles.",
      "impact": "A race can cross the Admin-to-Super-Admin authorization boundary, potentially permitting account takeover or administrative-role changes.",
      "locations": [
        {"file": "account/decorators.py", "start_line": 12, "end_line": 28},
        {"file": "account/decorators.py", "start_line": 41, "end_line": 44},
        {"file": "account/views/admin.py", "start_line": 46, "end_line": 76},
        {"file": "deploy/supervisord.conf", "start_line": 30, "end_line": 31}
      ],
      "source_snippets": [
        "return functools.partial(self.__call__, obj)",
        "self.request = args[1]",
        "if self.check_permission():",
        "return self.func(*args, **kwargs)",
        "user = self.request.user\n        return user.is_authenticated and user.is_super_admin()",
        "user.admin_type = data[\"admin_type\"]"
      ],
      "counterevidence": "The supplied Gunicorn command explicitly enables four threads, so concurrency is part of the deployed design. The exploit requires a suitable interleaving and a concurrent privileged call to the same decorator instance. Middleware independently requires an Admin for administrative URLs, so the strongest illustrated escalation begins with an Admin. No concurrency PoC was executed.",
      "remediation": "Make permission checks accept an invocation-local request argument and never store requests on shared decorator instances. A stateless function wrapper is sufficient."
    },
    {
      "title": "Arbitrary attachments execute active content on the authenticated application origin",
      "rule": "Isolate or force download of untrusted active uploads",
      "cwe": "CWE-434",
      "severity": "high",
      "confidence": "high",
      "attacker": "A limited Admin who uploads an HTML or SVG attachment and induces a Super Admin to open its returned public URL.",
      "invariant": "Uploaded attachments must not execute with the application origin and a more privileged viewer's session.",
      "source_to_sink": "SimditorFileUploadAPIView accepts a FileField, preserves any supplied extension, and writes the uploaded bytes to settings.UPLOAD_DIR. The returned URL is /public/upload/<generated-name><extension>. Nginx serves /public directly from /data using its MIME types, with no attachment disposition, sandbox, or separate origin. A valid .html document therefore executes attacker JavaScript with the application origin when opened. That script can make authenticated same-origin administrative requests as its viewer, including reading the CSRF cookie and supplying the required header.",
      "impact": "Stored active-content injection and escalation from limited Admin to a visiting Super Admin's application privileges.",
      "locations": [
        {"file": "utils/views.py", "start_line": 47, "end_line": 75},
        {"file": "utils/urls.py", "start_line": 5, "end_line": 7},
        {"file": "oj/settings.py", "start_line": 134, "end_line": 135},
        {"file": "deploy/nginx/locations.conf", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 3},
        {"file": "deploy/nginx/nginx.conf", "start_line": 12, "end_line": 15}
      ],
      "source_snippets": [
        "suffix = os.path.splitext(file.name)[-1].lower()\n        file_name = rand_str(10) + suffix",
        "with open(os.path.join(settings.UPLOAD_DIR, file_name), \"wb\") as f:",
        "\"file_path\": f\"{settings.UPLOAD_PREFIX}/{file_name}\",",
        "location /public {\n    root /data;\n}",
        "include /etc/nginx/mime.types;"
      ],
      "counterevidence": "Administrative middleware limits upload access to Admin roles and generated names prevent overwriting chosen files. Neither measure prevents active content at the returned URL. X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is present but does not stop a correctly named and served HTML document. The attack requires a privileged viewer to open the attachment.",
      "remediation": "Serve arbitrary attachments from an isolated origin without application cookies, or force downloads and apply a restrictive sandbox policy. Allow only explicitly supported passive formats for inline presentation."
    },
    {
      "title": "Fresh deployments expose a repository-known Super Admin password",
      "rule": "Do not provision a fixed privileged credential",
      "cwe": "CWE-1392",
      "severity": "high",
      "confidence": "high",
      "attacker": "An unauthenticated client reaching a fresh deployment before its initial administrator password has been changed.",
      "invariant": "A newly exposed installation must not have a universally known administrative login.",
      "source_to_sink": "The production entrypoint invokes inituser with a fixed username and fixed password. The command creates a Super Admin with all problem permissions when user ID 1 does not exist and hashes the supplied fixed password. Startup then launches the public application without requiring a credential change. The ordinary login endpoint accepts this account.",
      "impact": "Full application-administrator takeover of fresh or unchanged installations.",
      "locations": [
        {"file": "deploy/entrypoint.sh", "start_line": 61, "end_line": 64},
        {"file": "utils/management/commands/inituser.py", "start_line": 22, "end_line": 31},
        {"file": "account/views/oj.py", "start_line": 155, "end_line": 169},
        {"file": "init_db.sh", "start_line": 14, "end_line": 18}
      ],
      "source_snippets": [
        "python manage.py inituser",
        "if User.objects.filter(id=1).exists():",
        "user = User.objects.create(username=username, admin_type=AdminType.SUPER_ADMIN,\n                                       problem_permission=ProblemPermission.ALL)",
        "user.set_password(password)"
      ],
      "counterevidence": "The initializer does not overwrite an existing ID-1 user's changed password. Password hashing protects storage but does not change the universally known initial credential. Actual deployment password state was not inspected. The credential literal is intentionally omitted.",
      "remediation": "Require an operator-supplied initial secret or generate a one-time random secret and require setup before exposing privileged functionality."
    },
    {
      "title": "Disabled administrators retain access through existing sessions",
      "rule": "Enforce account disablement on every authenticated request",
      "cwe": "CWE-863",
      "severity": "medium",
      "confidence": "high",
      "attacker": "A previously authenticated Admin whose account is subsequently disabled.",
      "invariant": "Disabling an account must revoke its ability to perform protected operations.",
      "source_to_sink": "UserAdminAPI.put changes is_disabled without deleting sessions. AdminRoleRequiredMiddleware authorizes existing sessions using only is_authenticated and is_admin_role. Disablement is checked separately in BasePermissionDecorator, but many administrative handlers do not use that decorator. For example, ContestAPI.post can create a contest and ImportProblemAPI.post can import problems for a disabled administrator with an existing session. The custom User model uses is_disabled rather than the authentication backend's conventional is_active field.",
      "impact": "An account that an operator has disabled can continue creating and modifying application content and invoking upload/import functionality until its session expires.",
      "locations": [
        {"file": "account/views/admin.py", "start_line": 62, "end_line": 66},
        {"file": "account/middleware.py", "start_line": 36, "end_line": 41},
        {"file": "account/decorators.py", "start_line": 25, "end_line": 28},
        {"file": "contest/views/admin.py", "start_line": 24, "end_line": 41},
        {"file": "problem/views/admin.py", "start_line": 549, "end_line": 561}
      ],
      "source_snippets": [
        "user.is_disabled = data[\"is_disabled\"]",
        "if not (request.user.is_authenticated and request.user.is_admin_role()):",
        "if self.request.user.is_disabled:",
        "data[\"created_by\"] = request.user",
        "contest = Contest.objects.create(**data)"
      ],
      "counterevidence": "New password logins and API-key authentication reject disabled users; methods wrapped in BasePermissionDecorator also reject them. These controls do not cover already authenticated users entering unwrapped handlers.",
      "remediation": "Apply a single central disabled-account check before protected processing, and revoke active sessions when disabling an account."
    },
    {
      "title": "Contest helper authorizes rank viewing instead of contest administration",
      "rule": "Require ownership for administrative helper operations",
      "cwe": "CWE-862",
      "severity": "medium",
      "confidence": "high",
      "attacker": "An Admin with access to any suitable visible public contest, without ownership of the affected contest.",
      "invariant": "Only authorized contest administrators may inspect private participant identity fields or modify administrative rank annotations.",
      "source_to_sink": "ACMContestHelper uses check_contest_permission(check_type=\"ranks\"), which intentionally admits ordinary participants to started public contests. The enclosing middleware merely requires any Admin role. Its GET returns participant real names even to unrelated administrators. Its PUT then loads rank_id globally, without constraining the rank to self.contest, and saves caller-controlled checked state for problem_id. An attacker can authorize against one accessible contest and modify a rank belonging to another contest.",
      "impact": "Cross-contest modification of administrative verification annotations and unauthorized participant real-name disclosure.",
      "locations": [
        {"file": "contest/views/admin.py", "start_line": 162, "end_line": 194},
        {"file": "account/decorators.py", "start_line": 112, "end_line": 134},
        {"file": "contest/serializers.py", "start_line": 104, "end_line": 108}
      ],
      "source_snippets": [
        "@check_contest_permission(check_type=\"ranks\")",
        ".values(\"id\", \"user__username\", \"user__userprofile__real_name\", \"submission_info\")",
        "rank = ACMContestRank.objects.get(pk=data[\"rank_id\"])",
        "problem_rank_status[\"checked\"] = data[\"checked\"]\n        rank.save(update_fields=(\"submission_info\",))"
      ],
      "counterevidence": "The helper is behind the administrative middleware, and this operation changes the checked annotation rather than scores. The rank-viewing decorator validates visibility, passwords and contest timing, but none of these establishes administrative ownership of the loaded rank.",
      "remediation": "Require ensure_created_by(self.contest, request.user) for both methods and fetch the rank with contest=self.contest."
    },
    {
      "title": "Test-case ZIP uploads have no decompressed-size limit",
      "rule": "Bound archive expansion before allocating or writing its contents",
      "cwe": "CWE-409",
      "severity": "medium",
      "confidence": "high",
      "attacker": "An ordinary Admin able to call the test-case upload endpoint, including one without problem-management permission.",
      "invariant": "A bounded upload must not cause unbounded memory allocation or filesystem consumption.",
      "source_to_sink": "TestCaseAPI.post writes the uploaded archive and invokes process_zip without permission-specific checks or expanded-size limits. The processor selects predictable names such as 1.in, then zip_file.read decompresses each complete member into memory and .replace creates another bytes buffer before the content is written. Neither ZipInfo.file_size, aggregate expanded size, compression ratio, nor a per-account storage budget is checked. The Nginx 200M request limit constrains compressed input only.",
      "impact": "A small high-compression archive can exhaust a worker's memory or fill the shared data volume, disrupting judging and the application.",
      "locations": [
        {"file": "problem/views/admin.py", "start_line": 34, "end_line": 59},
        {"file": "problem/views/admin.py", "start_line": 147, "end_line": 159},
        {"file": "deploy/nginx/api_proxy.conf", "start_line": 4, "end_line": 4}
      ],
      "source_snippets": [
        "content = zip_file.read(f\"{dir}{item}\").replace(b\"\\r\\n\", b\"\\n\")",
        "f.write(content)",
        "info, test_case_id = self.process_zip(zip_file, spj=spj)",
        "client_max_body_size 200M;"
      ],
      "counterevidence": "The strict generated member names prevent ordinary ZIP traversal, and only Admin roles can access the endpoint. These controls do not bound decompression. No archive was generated or uploaded.",
      "remediation": "Reject archives exceeding per-member and aggregate expanded limits, enforce a bounded streaming decompression budget, clean up failed imports, and apply storage quotas."
    },

      "title": "Direct test-case pruning permits deletion outside the test-case directory",
      "rule": "Validate and contain direct filesystem identifiers",
      "cwe": "CWE-22",
      "severity": "medium",
      "confidence": "high",
      "attacker": "A malicious or compromised application Super Admin, whose application privileges do not inherently grant arbitrary host filesystem deletion.",
      "invariant": "The prune API may delete only eligible test-case directories beneath TEST_CASE_DIR.",
      "source_to_sink": "The DELETE handler passes the request id directly to delete_one. Unlike automatically enumerated orphan IDs, direct IDs are not matched against the alphanumeric identifier regex. delete_one joins the unvalidated value to TEST_CASE_DIR and recursively removes the resulting directory. A traversal or absolute path therefore escapes the intended storage root, subject only to the backend OS account's filesystem permissions.",
      "impact": "Recursive deletion of writable application data and other accessible directories beyond the intended test-case scope.",
      "locations": [
        {"file": "conf/views.py", "start_line": 186, "end_line": 208}
      ],
      "source_snippets": [

        "self.delete_one(test_case_id)",
        "test_case_re = re.compile(r\"^[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}$\")",
        "test_case_dir = os.path.join(settings.TEST_CASE_DIR, id)",
        "shutil.rmtree(test_case_dir, ignore_errors=True)"

      "counterevidence": "A Super Admin permission check is present. The automatic orphan enumeration validates identifiers, but the direct-id branch bypasses it. The operation runs with the backend account's permissions, not automatically with host root privileges. No destructive operation was performed.",
      "remediation": "Require a full-match valid test-case identifier for every branch, resolve and verify containment under TEST_CASE_DIR, and require membership in the eligible orphan set before deletion."

A source reader obtains the credential outside Travis and can potentially use the associated notification integration.",
